title: Remote-Work Stipend Refresh That Straddles the Policy Change
scenario_text:
Corvus Media provides a remote-work equipment stipend under its Remote Work Policy.

Version 1 (in effect through 2024-12-31): "Eligible employees receive a $1,000 equipment stipend, refreshable once every 24 months measured from the employee's enrollment (grant) date."

Version 2 (effective 2025-01-01): "The equipment stipend is $1,500, refreshable every 36 months measured from the enrollment (grant) date." v2 includes a transition clause: "A stipend's amount and refresh eligibility run from the employee's enrollment (grant) date under the version in force on that date. Enrollments dated before January 1, 2025 keep the v1 $1,000 amount and 24-month cycle for that enrollment period; the v2 $1,500 amount and 36-month cycle apply only to grants (including refresh grants) dated on or after January 1, 2025. The new policy does not retroactively extend or increase an in-progress enrollment."

The HR benefits system shows employee E-2255: initial stipend enrollment (grant) dated 2023-08-15, amount $1,000 paid; no refresh yet.

E-2255 messages HR benefits in Slack on 2025-01-08: "Now that the stipend is $1,500 on a 36-month cycle, does my clock reset to 36 months, and when can I get my next refresh, and will it be $1,000 or $1,500?"

Using the policy history, the transition clause, and the benefits record, determine E-2255's next refresh eligibility date and the amount of that next grant.
question: When is E-2255 next eligible for a stipend refresh, and what amount will that next grant be?
